items.title: Duffy Jackson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 17, 1995
items.q: Stan Kenton really took it to some other more academic concepts at the collegiate level.

ctx.x: And you know I would love to have a show in today’s scheme of things, you know this was before Sesame Street or any of the young kid shows. And my dad always, he was a pioneer of jazz education for the young kids in the schools you know. Stan Kenton really took it to some other more academic concepts at the collegiate level. But as far as just you know, playing jazz for children in the school, my dad did that in the late 40s. You

know “Bop Goes to School” — my dad had the first jazz band to ever go to a high school and play for the kids. Now I don’t know if maybe other people did it before, but my dad actually documented that in the late 40s.
